correctness.rationale: Set P_a on [0,b] and Q on (b,1], with d>=1, 0<c<b/d^2, b<=a<1. For a>b the branches alternate, and the 2-step return G_a=Q o P_a is a contraction with uniform derivative <=cd²/b<1. Its unique left fixed point xi_a and right partner eta_a attract every orbit by parity, and Cesaro convergence plus invariance characterizes the unique Borel invariant measure. At the endpoint a=b, the continuous extension G_b fixes zero but the actual convention maps 0→b→1→c; every positive left coordinate contracts towards zero, every orbit has omega={0,b}, and the universal empirical limit nu=(delta0+delta_b)/2 is noninvariant because F_b(b)=1. Dominated convergence rules out any invariant Borel probability. Uniform F_a→F_b, weak mu_a→nu, and for d>1 xi_a~c((a-b)/(1-b))^d and multiplier~(cd²/b)((a-b)/(1-b))^(d-1) follow from the fixed-point identity and derivative product. Independently exact rational test at b=3/4,c=1/16,d=2 confirmed 0→b→1→c and positive return contraction; representative supercritical cycles independently converged. Finite orbits do not prove measure claims.
